rdf:Description.rdfs:label: gitoid
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [Gitoid](https://www.iana.org/assignments/uri-schemes/prov/gitoid), stands for [Git Object ID](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-Objects). A gitoid of type blob is a unique hash of a binary artifact. A gitoid may represent either an [Artifact Identifier](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-identifier-types) for the software artifact or an [Input Manifest Identifier](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#input-manifest-identifier) for the software artifact's associated [Artifact Input Manifest](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-input-manifest); this ambiguity exists because the Artifact Input Manifest is itself an artifact, and the gitoid of that artifact is its valid identifier. Gitoids calculated on software artifacts (Snippet, File, or Package Elements) should be recorded in the SPDX 3 SoftwareArtifact's contentIdentifier property. Gitoids calculated on the Artifact Input Manifest (Input Manifest Identifier) should be recorded in the SPDX 3 Element's externalIdentifier property. See [OmniBOR Specification](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/), a minimalistic specification for describing software [Artifact Dependency Graphs](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-dependency-graph-adg).

The location for dropping off or delivering a package or item.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A formal standard is a standard ratified by a recognized standards-development organization and published as a normative reference.
The AssemblyProcess represents the process of creating a product by assembling a set of components, potentially in a way that allows for at disassembly (at least partially).

Temporary endeavor with a beginning and an end and that must be used to create a unique product, service or result.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: regulation

A specification is a detailed description of the design, requirements, or features of a product, process, or system.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: deviceDriver
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element represents software that controls hardware devices.
EvaluationResultType describes the outcome of an evaluation or verification process with.
EvidenceRelationship defines the association between pieces of evidence and EvaluationResult.

A contact point from an Artifact to an Agent.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: BLAKE2b algorithm with a digest size of 384, as defined in [RFC 7693](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc7693/) Section 4.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Captured datastream like audio, video, or any other kind of continuous electronic capture of events, behavior or conditions.
A property name with an associated value.
Specifies a time when a vulnerability assessment was modified
Specifies the CVSS vector string for a vulnerability.
The name of a relevant standard that may apply to an artifact.
Specifies a vulnerability and its associated information.
Location of a specific action.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: specification
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a plan, guideline or strategy how to create, perform or analyze an application.
The provider of a SoftwareService.
Methods that can be used to explain the results from the AI model.
A collection of Elements that have a shared context.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: structured
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Data is stored in tabular format or retrieved from a relational database.
A collection of SPDX Elements that could potentially be serialized.
Class that describes an instance of Hardware.
Provide context for a relationship that occurs in the lifecycle.
Location is used to define the location, address or coordinates of a place.
Sets the context for an assessment by specifying the related project.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: doesNotAffect
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Vulnerability has no impact on each `to` Element. The use of the `doesNotAffect` is constrained to `VexNotAffectedVulnAssessmentRelationship` classed relationships.
UnitofMeasure specify information structures through industry standards for Units of Measure, Quantity Kinds, Dimensions and Data Types.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: operatingSystem
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is an operating system.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: limitedSupport

A key with an associated value.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: any hashing algorithm that does not exist in this list of entries
Identifies when the Element was originally created.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: file
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a single file which can be independently distributed (configuration file, statically linked binary, Kubernetes deployment, etc.).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: staticAnalysisReport
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a static analysis report for a package.
An entity providing an assessment.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: ai
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The element follows the AI profile specification.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: module
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a module of a piece of software.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM generated through instrumenting the system running the software, to capture only components present in the system, as well as external call-outs or dynamically loaded components. In some contexts, this may also be referred to as an "Instrumented" or "Dynamic" SBOM.
Records the biases that the dataset is known to encompass.
Class that describes a physical instance of Hardware.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Other exploit catalogs.
Enumeration of verification types.
Quantity is the amount in the selected QUDT unit.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: locatedAt
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: `from` element located at a specific `to` location. A time period is optional.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: modifiedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element is modified by each `to` Element.
A distinct article or unit within the domain.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: duns
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [Data Universal Numbering System (D-U-N-S) Number](https://www.dnb.com/en-us/smb/duns.html) is a unique nine-digit identifier, issued by Dun & Bradstreet, that identifies a business entity, often on a location-specific basis.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: custody
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Custody refers to the responsibility, control, and safekeeping of an asset, person, or legal entity. It involves both physical possession and legal authority over something or someone.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: implementedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Requirement is implemented in the `to` Element(s).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: deployed
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: In addition to being supported by the supplier, the software is known to have been deployed and is in use. For a software as a service provider, this implies the software is now available as a service.
The category describes the hardware item in a DefinedType.
A license that is not listed on the SPDX License List.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: trainedOn
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element has been trained on the `to` Element(s).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: x509Cert
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to an X.509 certificate as defined in [RFC 1422](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc1422/). The media type shall be one of application/x-x509-ca-cert or application/x-x509-user-cert.
Information related to hardware dimension.
The location for picking up a package or item.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: log
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Time-stamped records capturing system or operational data recorded as usually as a response to specific triggers in a specified environment.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A value used in a key-value pair with a generic key that refers to an Element

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: qualityAssessmentReport
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a quality assessment for a package.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: act
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The vulnerability requires attention from the organization's internal, supervisory-level and leadership-level individuals. Necessary actions include requesting assistance or information about the vulnerability, as well as publishing a notification either internally and/or externally. Typically, internal groups would meet to determine the overall response and then execute agreed upon actions. CISA recommends remediating Act vulnerabilities as soon as possible.
This is the agent that performed the act of destroying the item.
Information related to hardware dimension.
A distinct article or unit related to Software.
EvaluationResult is the result of an evaluation.
Protocols which support authentication.
The name of the recipient expressed in text.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: expandedLicensing
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The element follows the ExpandedLicensing profile specification.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: securityOther
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to related security information of unspecified type.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: componentNotPresent
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The software is not affected because the vulnerable component is not in the product.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: archive
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is an archived collection of one or more files (.tar, .zip, etc.).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: trackStar
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: ("Track\*" in the SSVC spec) The vulnerability contains specific characteristics that may require closer monitoring for changes. CISA recommends remediating Track\* vulnerabilities within standard update timelines.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: container
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a container image which can be used by a container runtime application.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: draft
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: in production
An out of specification action is defined in this class.
Describes if a given file is a directory or non-directory kind of file.
Provides additional purpose information of the software artifact.

**DEPRECATED in SPDX 3.1.** Use [customIdToLicense](./customIdToLicense.md) instead.

**NOTE:** This property is deprecated and only included for backward compatibility. New documents should use [customIdToLicense](./customIdToLicense.md) instead.
Class that describes an action that has occurred.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: obsolete
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: superseded or not valid at present
Assessment of an Element for export control classification.
Refers to one or more Elements that are part of an ElementCollection.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: complete
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The relationship is known to be exhaustive.
A key used in a generic key-value pair.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: vcs
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a version control system related to a software artifact.

It is the authoritative or credible entity, document, or body of knowledge that provides the meaning of an additionalInformation key and/or its values, ensuring accuracy, context, and standardization.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: nuget
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a NuGet package. The package locator format is defined in the [NuGet documentation](https://docs.nuget.org) and looks like `package/version`.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: inlineMitigationsAlreadyExist
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Built-in inline controls or mitigations prevent an adversary from leveraging the vulnerability.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: test
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relationship has specific context implications during an element's testing phase, during development.
The measure of length refers to the dimension of an object or space that describes how long it is, typically expressed in various units depending on the system of measurement being used.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: riskAssessment
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a risk assessment for a package.
A reference to a resource identifier defined outside the scope of SPDX 3 content that uniquely identifies an Element.
Identifies who or what supplied the artifact or VulnAssessmentRelationship referenced by the Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: update
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A relationship has specific context implications for a product update.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: registration
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Dataset is not publicly available and an email registration is required before accessing the dataset, although without an affirmative acceptance of terms.
Class that describes a build instance of software/artifacts.
Use Process defines actions used by elements.
The CreateProcess refers to the abstract process class that can be used to represent the process of creation of a product.
An Individual Value for License where the SPDX data creator determines that no license is present.
Abstract class for additional text intended to be added to a License, but which is not itself a standalone License.
A canonical, unique, immutable identifier.
Identifier for product production batch.
A probability score between 0 and 1 of a vulnerability being exploited.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: video
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Data is video based, such as a collection of movie clips featuring Tom Hanks.
A canonical, unique, immutable identifier of the artifact content, that may be used for verifying its identity and/or integrity.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: framework
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a software framework.
Provides the location for more information regarding an external identifier.
A Package that contains AI software or an AI model.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: delegatedTo
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Agent is delegating an action to the Agent of the `to` Relationship (which shall be of type invokedBy), during a LifecycleScopeType (e.g. the `to` invokedBy Relationship is being done on behalf of `from`).
Refers to any unit of content that can be associated with a distribution of software.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: sha256
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SHA-2 with a digest length of 256, as defined in [RFC 6234](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc6234/).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: metrics
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to metrics related to package such as OpenSSF scorecards.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: evidence
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is the evidence that a specification or requirement has been fulfilled.
Identifies the full text of a License or Addition.
Version identifier for the hardware product.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: attend
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The vulnerability requires attention from the organization's internal, supervisory-level individuals. Necessary actions include requesting assistance or information about the vulnerability, and may involve publishing a notification either internally and/or externally. CISA recommends remediating Attend vulnerabilities sooner than standard update timelines.
Defines the version of a specific process.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: contains
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element contains each `to` Element.
This individual element was defined by the spec.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: copiedTo
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element has been copied to each `to` Element.
Capture the scope of information about a specific relationship between elements.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: low
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: When a CVSS score is between 0.1 - 3.9.
Provides information about the primary purpose of the software artifact.
Refers to any object that stores content on a computer.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: phoneNumber
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Phone number; A string of decimal digits that uniquely indicates the network termination point defined in [RFC 3966](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc3966/) Section 5.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: All other simulation types.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: serious
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The highest level of risk posed by an AI system.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: other
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Any other specialized or custom verification method that fits the context.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: swid
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Concise Software Identification (CoSWID) tag, as defined in [RFC 9393](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9393/) Section 2.3.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: inspection
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A thorough examination or checking of documentation, records, processes, or systems to confirm compliance or adherence. An inspection needs to have a defined set of acceptance criteria (e.g. a checklist), a documentation of roles involved in the inspection (e.g. to document the inspector's independence) and a clear documentation of when and how it was performed.
A collection of Elements, not necessarily with unifying context.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: demonstration
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Demonstrating and monitoring or recording that the item under verification to confirm that a requirement is met by the item under verification.
A short description of an Element.
Links a vulnerability and one or more elements designating the latter as products not affected by the vulnerability.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: partialAutomation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Level 2 - Partial automation or task automation. Some sub-functions of the system are fully automated while the system remain under control of an external agent. The system can perform actions for an approved task without requiring the agent's continuous direct control.
Unit in which energy is measured.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A buildType is a hint that is used to indicate the toolchain, platform, or infrastructure that the build was invoked on.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: packagedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Every `to` Element is a packaged instance of the `from` Element (`from` packagedBy `to`).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: fixedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Designates a `from` Vulnerability has been fixed by the `to` Agent(s).
A reference to a resource outside the scope of SPDX 3 content related to an Element.
A collection of SPDX Elements describing a single package.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: query
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Dataset is publicly available, but not all at once, and can only be accessed through queries which return parts of the dataset.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: mailingList
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to the mailing list used by the maintainer for a package.
Provides an independently reproducible mechanism that permits verification of a specific Element.
Specifies the algorithm used for calculating the hash value.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: releaseHistory
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a published list of releases for a package.
Confidentiality level of the data points contained in the dataset.
An inspection action refers to a specific activity or set of activities performed during an inspection to examine, verify, or evaluate an item, process, or system.
Energy consumption incurred by an AI model.
Specifies a country code of the location.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: follows
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `to` Element succeeds the `from` Element, establishing a unidirectional sequence. This succession is defined as chronological, procedural, or logical. It is used to represent either a temporal order (e.g., in a workflow) or a logical order for processing and traversal (e.g., in an ordered list).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasResolution
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` ResolutionAction point to the `to` OutOfSpecAction that is addressed.
Type of support that is associated with an artifact.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: executable
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is an Artifact that can be run on a computer.
RequirementVerification class defines the base properties of a verification.
An SPDX version 2.X compatible verification method for software packages.
Provides a CVSS version 3 assessment for a vulnerability.
A substitute for a URI.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: audit
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: An examination typically focusing on compliance with policies, standards, or regulations. Usually this is done during an audit meeting, while the assessment also involves deep and detailed reviews of work products (e.g. requirements, verification specifications, reports etc.)

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: observation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Documentation of direct monitoring or witnessing of the demonstration of processes, tests, or any kind of system responses during a specified timeframe under specified environmental conditions.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: securityThreatModel
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference the [security threat model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threat_model) for a package.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: yes
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Indicates presence of the field.
A map of Element identifiers that are used within an SpdxDocument but defined external to that SpdxDocument.
This is the planned individual, business, or organization who was previously managing goods, services, or assets.
Country for which export controls must be taken into account.
Information related to physical hardware.
Describes if any sensitive personal information is present in the dataset.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: analyzed
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM generated through analysis of artifacts (e.g., executables, packages, containers, and virtual machine images) after its build. Such analysis generally requires a variety of heuristics. In some contexts, this may also be referred to as a "3rd party" SBOM.
A license addition that is not listed on the SPDX Exceptions List.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: amendedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element is amended by each `to` Element.
Abstract class for the portion of an AnyLicenseInfo representing a license.

rdf:Description.sh:message: https://spdx.org/rdf/3.1/terms/SupplyChain/UseAction is an abstract class and should not be instantiated directly. Instantiate a subclass instead.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: noSupport
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: There is no support for the artifact from the supplier, consumer assumes any support obligations.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: vulnerabilityExploitabilityAssessment
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to a Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange (VEX) statement which provides information on whether a product is impacted by a specific vulnerability in an included package and, if affected, whether there are actions recommended to remediate. See also [NTIA VEX one-page summary](https://ntia.gov/files/ntia/publications/vex_one-page_summary.pdf).
An assertion made in relation to one or more elements.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: republishedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Designates a `from` Vulnerability's details were tracked, aggregated, and/or enriched to improve context (i.e. NVD) by each `to` Agent.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: test
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a test used to verify functionality on a software element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: cpe23
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [Common Platform Enumeration: Naming Specification Version 2.3](https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/detail/nistir/7695/final).
Information about the relationship between two Elements.

**DEPRECATED in SPDX 3.1.** Use [/Software/artifactSize](../../Software/Properties/artifactSize.md) instead.
Size of the dataset.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasPrerequisite
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element has a prerequisite on each `to` Element, during a LifecycleScopeType period.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element refers to a disk image that can be written to a disk, booted in a VM, etc. A disk image typically contains most or all of the components necessary to boot, such as bootloaders, kernels, firmware, userspace, etc.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: fullAutomation
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Level 5 - Full automation. The system is capable of performing its entire mission without external intervention.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: publishedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Designates a `from` Vulnerability was made available for public use or reference by each `to` Agent.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: invokedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element was invoked by the `to` Agent, during a LifecycleScopeType period (for example, a Build element that describes a build step).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: inconclusive
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Inconclusive refers to a result or outcome from a verification, test, or analysis that cannot be clearly classified as either positive (successful, pass) or negative (failed, reject). An inconclusive result means there was not enough clear evidence, data, or signal to make a definitive determination, and further investigation or additional testing is necessary. An inconclusive result always shall need a comment on it.

rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A `from` Vulnerability has been fixed in each `to` Element. The use of the `fixedIn` type is constrained to `VexFixedVulnAssessmentRelationship` classed relationships.

A gitoid may represent either an [Artifact Identifier](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-identifier-types) for the software artifact or an [Input Manifest Identifier](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#input-manifest-identifier) for the software artifact's associated [Artifact Input Manifest](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-input-manifest); this ambiguity exists because the Artifact Input Manifest is itself an artifact, and the gitoid of that artifact is its valid identifier. Gitoids calculated on software artifacts (Snippet, File, or Package Elements) should be recorded in the SPDX 3 SoftwareArtifact's contentIdentifier property. Gitoids calculated on the Artifact Input Manifest (Input Manifest Identifier) should be recorded in the SPDX 3 Element's externalIdentifier property. See [OmniBOR Specification](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/), a minimalistic specification for describing software [Artifact Dependency Graphs](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-dependency-graph-adg).
